question: Which major African health agreement sets the spending target that Nigeria's public health budget often fails to reach?
explanation: Nigerian health budgets consistently fall short of the fifteen percent target agreed upon by African leaders in Abuja. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T3#BMP322_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why do public health clinics in Nigeria often run out of basic drugs and medical equipment?

options.A: Excessive international donor funding causing waste
options.B: Complete elimination of private sector pharmacies
options.C: Zero demand for maternal health services
options.D: Inadequate public funding and low budget allocation

explanation: When governments fail to adequately finance the health sector, facilities cannot purchase essential medical commodities. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T3#BMP322_U2_T3_h1)

question: What does 'out-of-pocket expenditure' mean in healthcare?

options.A: Direct payment for services at the point of care without insurance
options.B: Government reimbursement paid directly to the patient's family
options.C: Monthly salary deductions made automatically for civil servants
options.D: Free medical care funded entirely through foreign donor grants

explanation: Out-of-pocket spending happens when cash is handed over immediately to pay for drugs, tests, or procedures. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T3#BMP322_U2_T3_h2)

question: A pregnant woman with severe bleeding stays at home because her family has no cash for transport and hospital fees. What financial barrier is this?
explanation: Requiring cash payment at the exact time of service creates a deadly delay for obstetric emergencies. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T3#BMP322_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is the main goal of the National Health Insurance Scheme in Nigeria?

options.A: To generate profit for private pharmaceutical companies
options.B: To replace traditional birth attendants with modern surgeons
options.C: To provide social health security and affordable care for all
options.D: To fund international medical tourism for government workers

explanation: The health insurance scheme was created to protect citizens from financial ruin due to medical bills. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T3#BMP322_U2_T3_h3)

question: How does risk pooling protect individuals within a health insurance system?

options.A: Hospitals waive all charges for patients who wait until weekends
options.B: Contributions from many people cover the high medical costs of the few who fall sick
options.C: The government refunds all transport money spent visiting a clinic
options.D: Every patient pays the exact full cost of their own surgery in advance

explanation: Pooling spreads financial risk across a large group, preventing one severe illness from destroying a family financially. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T3#BMP322_U2_T3_h3)

question: Which of these services is normally NOT covered under standard maternal health insurance benefits?

options.A: Cosmetic plastic surgery for personal enhancement
options.B: Antenatal care visits and routine clinical checkups

explanation: Health insurance covers medically necessary care, not cosmetic procedures. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T3#BMP322_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why do insured pregnant women sometimes still spend their own money at accredited clinics?

options.A: The insurance scheme covers all private luxury hotel rooms
options.B: Facilities may lack basic consumables and ask patients to buy them
options.C: National laws forbid hospitals from using insurance cards
options.D: Midwives collect cash bonuses for every delivery performed

explanation: Supply chain failures often force clinics to tell insured patients to purchase essential delivery items out of pocket. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T3#BMP322_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why do many primary health clinics struggle to take part in health insurance programs?

options.A: They lack minimum infrastructure, staffing, and drug supplies for accreditation
options.B: Rural communities completely reject free medical services
options.C: Doctors refuse to let midwives handle insurance paperwork
options.D: They receive too much money and do not know how to spend it

explanation: Without basic structural standards, primary clinics cannot pass accreditation to receive and manage insurance funds. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T3#BMP322_U2_T3_h5)

question: When is the best time for a midwife to educate a pregnant woman about registering for health insurance?

options.A: During emergency resuscitation in the labor ward
options.D: Immediately after the baby is discharged home

explanation: Early antenatal education gives families time to understand and enroll in financing schemes before delivery approaches. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T3#BMP322_U2_T3_h6)

question: A woman arrives in labor at a clinic operating under an insurance scheme, but she has no cash or card. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Provide necessary emergency care while exploring equity funds or waivers
options.B: Wait for her relatives to travel home and sell property for cash
options.C: Turn her away immediately until she pays cash deposit for supplies
options.D: Refuse to examine her until an insurance card is presented

explanation: Professional ethics and vulnerable fund policies require prioritizing life-saving care while working out financial pathways. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T3#BMP322_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of subsidized equity funds in maternal health financing?

options.A: To build luxury private hospitals for wealthy politicians
options.B: To pay insurance premiums for vulnerable pregnant women and children
options.C: To pay high salaries exclusively to specialist obstetricians
options.D: To purchase foreign vehicles for hospital administrators

explanation: Equity funds protect the poorest mothers by covering their insurance costs so they can access care for free. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T3#BMP322_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why is expanding health insurance coverage to the informal sector so important in Nigeria?

options.A: Informal sector workers refuse to visit hospitals under any circumstance
options.B: Government revenue comes exclusively from agricultural exports
options.C: Formal sector workers already receive free healthcare abroad
options.D: The vast majority of the Nigerian workforce earns their living outside formal government jobs

explanation: Since most Nigerians work in informal trades, leaving them uninsured leaves the majority unprotected from high medical bills. [learn more](BMP322_U2_T3#BMP322_U2_T3_h7)
